title: Add central neon style constants and quality config
description:
Add a central STYLE constants object for all neon arcade colors and visual settings, plus a quality config for disabling expensive effects. Do not change gameplay logic.
Implemented: Added central STYLE and QUALITY config and routed existing visual defaults through it without gameplay changes.
acceptance_criteria: A single central STYLE object defines the dark background colors, cyan player color, blue cube color, red hazard color, ground line color, UI colors, alpha values, stroke widths, light sizes, particle caps, and timing values.
A quality config exists and can independently disable lightmap, particles, player trail, background motion, and screen shake.
The constants are available to render/effect code without coupling them to physics or collision logic.
Gameplay behavior, object spawning, collision geometry, score behavior, and menu behavior are unchanged.
A screenshot is saved at screenshots/TASK-001.png before marking this task to-verify.
test_steps: Open index.html in a browser or run a local static server and open the game.
Start both classic and bad versions and confirm the game still starts and plays.
Confirm the browser console has no new errors.
Capture a screenshot and save it as screenshots/TASK-001.png.
Confirm screenshots/TASK-001.png exists.

title: Introduce isolated renderer and effects classes
description: Add dedicated visual-only classes for background rendering, lightmap rendering, particles, player trail, screen effects, and UI styling hooks. Keep these classes easy to disable and separate from gameplay logic.
acceptance_criteria: Background, lightmap, particles, player trail, screen effects, and UI styling each live in their own class or clearly isolated module.
The new classes expose small draw/update-style methods and read game state without owning physics, collision, spawning, or scoring decisions.
Each visual feature can be bypassed through STYLE or quality config.
Existing gameplay behavior remains unchanged.
A screenshot is saved at screenshots/TASK-002.png before marking this task to-verify.
test_steps: Open index.html in a browser or run a local static server and open the game.
Start both classic and bad versions and confirm gameplay still works.

Confirm the browser console has no new errors.

title: Compare bad version screenshots against concept art
description: Open the game with bad version, play it, make screenshots, place them into screenshots/TASK-017, then compare the result with /opt/grapnelninja/screenshots/concept_art.png. If the result differs drastically from the concept art, add more pending tickets to tasks.json describing the missing visual work.
acceptance_criteria: The bad version is opened and played long enough to show player movement, cubes/platforms, triangle hazards, ground line, background, lighting, particles/trails, and UI.
Multiple screenshots are saved under screenshots/TASK-017/.
The screenshots are compared against /opt/grapnelninja/screenshots/concept_art.png for overall style, palette, neon outlines, lighting, background geometry, UI treatment, and readability.
If the result differs drastically from the concept art, new pending follow-up tickets are appended to tasks.json with clear acceptance criteria and test steps.
If the result is close enough to the concept art, the task description is updated with a one-line note explaining that no follow-up tickets were needed.
test_steps: Open index.html in a browser or run a local static server and open the game.
Select bad version and play for at least 30 seconds.
Capture multiple representative screenshots during play and save them under screenshots/TASK-017/.
Confirm screenshots/TASK-017/ exists and contains the captured screenshots.
Open /opt/grapnelninja/screenshots/concept_art.png and compare it with the captured screenshots.
If the result differs drastically, append new pending follow-up tickets to tasks.json before marking this task to-verify.
Confirm tasks.json remains valid JSON.
